title: Invited: Algorithm and Hardware Co-Design for Energy-Efficient Neural SLAM
problem: Neural network-based SLAM systems require high computational resources and energy consumption, limiting deployment in resource-constrained robotics and autonomous systems. The challenge is to optimize both algorithm and hardware architecture jointly for efficient neural SLAM execution.
motivation: Enabling practical neural SLAM for energy-constrained embedded systems such as robots and autonomous vehicles requires co-optimization across algorithm compression and specialized hardware design.
method: The approach combines model compression techniques to reduce neural network computational demands with customized hardware architecture design. Micro-architectural optimizations and dataflow optimizations are applied to improve computational efficiency and performance. Compressed neural SLAM models are executed on specialized hardware to achieve improved energy efficiency.
key_novelty: Co-design of model compression algorithms with specialized hardware micro-architecture and optimized dataflow specifically tailored for neural SLAM systems.
contributions: Model compression techniques for neural SLAM networks
Customized hardware architecture with micro-architectural optimizations
Dataflow optimizations for neural SLAM acceleration
Energy-efficient neural SLAM system design and evaluation
limitations: Specific technical details, quantitative metrics, baseline comparisons, and experimental results are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Algorithm-hardware co-design for energy-efficient neural SLAM
